verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB), and when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more ... or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; §6 last connection deletes WAL and shm; Litestream: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB'

verdicts.claim: All automatic checkpoints and plain sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() calls are PASSIVE; never invoke the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.2: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; c3ref: busy-handler 'is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint can run alongside readers but must stop at any WAL frame past a current reader's end mark; records progress in wal-index
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.2: 'the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader ... remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'

verdicts.claim: The WAL is reset only when the checkpoint has transferred and synced the entire WAL and no reader uses it; a write that starts mid-checkpoint stops reset
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.2 reset conditions quoted; mid-checkpoint write part only from Syncthing forum user (Audrius, 2025-04-02): 'If there is a write after checkpoint started, it can't be finished' — not stated by sqlite.org

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL the checkpoint is the only operation that syncs; with FULL, writers also sync the WAL each commit
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.3: 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation'; 'Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL'

verdicts.claim: Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15) WAL size for a single transaction is proportional; >1 GB transactions may fail with I/O or disk-full error
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself'; §1: 'in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may fail with an I/O or disk-full error' (c3ref page does not mention this)

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint modes PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE semantics; FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE block new writers not readers and invoke busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref FULL: 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns three columns; col1=1 if blocked; cols 2,3 -1 without WAL; NOOP; after TRUNCATE both counts 0
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns'; 'second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'; c3ref: after TRUNCATE 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs PASSIVE checkpoints by default (min-checkpoint-page-count 1000, checkpoint-interval 1m), TRUNCATE fallback at truncate-page-n 121,359; v0.5.15
verdicts.evidence: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB'; 'truncate-page-n bounds WAL growth rather than guaranteeing the -wal file shrinks'; 'Set truncate-page-n: 0'; 'v0.5.15 Crossing the truncate-page-n threshold no longer forces a blocking checkpoint immediately'

verdicts.claim: Read performance degrades as WAL grows (proportional); checkpoints slower than writes; trade-off; separate thread avoids blocking on sync
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.3: 'time needed to check the WAL file is proportional to the size of the WAL file'; 'make checkpoints slower than write transactions'; 'run the periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process'

verdicts.claim: SQLite's autocheckpoint does not prevent unbounded WAL growth in a busy database; apps may need own checkpoints (dedicated thread or sqlite3_wal_hook)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6 starvation: 'always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; §3.1 sqlite3_wal_hook callback; Guix source returned HTTP 502 (not checked)

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: overlapping readers never leave a gap, WAL grows without bound; docs suggest reader gaps or RESTART/TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'ensuring that there are "reader gaps"'; 'running manual checkpoints with the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART or SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE ... readers might block'

verdicts.claim: Busy handler returns 0 -> falls back to PASSIVE and returns SQLITE_BUSY; checkpoint lock held -> SQLITE_BUSY without busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case'; 'Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case'

verdicts.claim: Completed checkpoint does not shrink the WAL; rewinds and overwrites unless journal_size_limit (default -1) or TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)'; pragma.html: 'default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; truncates 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets'

verdicts.claim: A large single write transaction cannot be reset mid-transaction, so the WAL can grow very big until it commits
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction ... in the meantime, the file can grow very big'

verdicts.claim: Syncthing reported WAL growth to multiple GB; timer-based checkpointer never found a quiet window; competes with auto-checkpoints; no fix confirmed
verdicts.evidence: 'we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'; 'As checkpoints of any kind are exclusive, we're blocking our own checkpointer'; posts dated 2026-02-06; fixes only proposed. 'large-folder syncs' wording not seen verbatim

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug present 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, fixed 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7; not an emergency
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §11: 'present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; §11.2 'this is not an emergency'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: SQLite page says fixed in 3.51.3; the blog reports the fix as 3.53.0 and says it tested that build
verdicts.evidence: blog: 'the version built against SQLite 3.53.0 (where the bug is fixed)'; built from sqlite-amalgamation-3530000.zip; no mention of 3.51.3

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: SQLite WAL page lists only PASSIVE, FULL and RESTART as subtypes in 3.2 but mentions TRUNCATE elsewhere
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.2: 'There are three subtypes of checkpoints ... PASSIVE, FULL, and RESTART'; §6 names SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE
